meta.what: Round 6 C1 + C4. (C1) Buyers of the 'Rest of world' Russian arms income in russian_arms_exports.json, per country, in the same structure as that file's country entries, so they can be merged; a smaller ROW remains. (C4) The Iran overlap between military_to_russia (flowback2.json) and Iran's payments for Russian arms.
meta.units: EUR bn nominal per year; 2026 = Jan-Aug, not annualised. Payments set in EUR; expected levels set in USD and converted with ECB annual averages as in russian_arms_exports.json (2022 1.05304, 2023 1.08126, 2024 1.08238, 2025 1.12998, 2026 1.16285).
meta.method: Payments per buyer from contract reports and SIPRI regional shares (fact sheets 2024-2026; the SIPRI database backend refused connections on 2026-10-18, as in round 5), constrained to sum to no more than the old ROW in every year. Ranges: multipliers on central (0.3-2.5x for guesses, 0.4-2.0x with a contract anchor, 0.6-1.5x for Bulgaria). change = expected - actual; range in quadrature, same formula as russian_arms_exports.json. in_customs zero for all (no arms seen in these buyers' customs); Bulgaria/Slovakia maintenance may be in services data.
meta.recommended_use: Replace countries.ROW of russian_arms_exports.json with countries.ROW here and add the other ISO3 entries as new buyers (none of them exists in russian_arms_exports.json). National totals are unchanged. Apply iran_overlap: add overlap_eur_bn central to IRN change_vs_expected_ex_customs (range: low/high of the overlap).

iran_overlap.what: Value counted twice for Iran: drones/missiles sent to Russia (flowback2.json military_to_russia, toward Russia) that also settled Iran's payments for Russian arms (russian_arms_exports.json IRN payments, counted as money paid to Russia).
iran_overlap.recommended_side: Subtract from russian_arms_exports IRN (payments and change_vs_expected_ex_customs, i.e. add the overlap to the change), keep military_to_russia unchanged. Do NOT move the subtracted amount to other buyers or ROW.
iran_overlap.method: overlap_y = barter share x Iran's central payment to Russia in year y (russian_arms_exports.json). Cumulative overlap is always below cumulative Iranian deliveries to Russia minus what Russia demonstrably paid in cash/gold (EUR 140m cash Aug 2022; ~2.07 t gold Feb 2023 ~EUR 0.11bn), so the cap never binds.

overlaps: (1) russian_arms_exports.json: these entries REPLACE its ROW; national totals and the 19 named buyers are unchanged, so nothing is added on top. None of the 18 new ISO3 codes exists there. (2) trade_full.json / nonreport.json: arms are outside customs for all these buyers (in_customs = 0). Libya, Venezuela, Sudan are non-reporters corrected in nonreport.json from tanker/partner data; arms are not in those corrections. (3) Services (BaTiS/Eurostat): Bulgaria's and Slovakia's MiG-29 maintenance (EUR 0.006-0.012bn/yr) may sit in 'maintenance and repair' imports from Russia; if the builder's services part shows a fall in that line for BGR/SVK, drop these two entries. (4) Wagner/Africa Corps service fees (Mali ~USD 0.13bn/yr) and gold/mining concessions are not included anywhere here and, as far as checked, not in other files (companies_all, kgz_gold are unrelated); they are an open item, not part of arms revenue. (5) Iran: military_to_russia (flowback2.json) vs IRN payments (russian_arms_exports.json): see iran_overlap; subtract once from the IRN arms payments. Separately, an Iranian MP claimed missiles/drones were bartered for Russian grain: if true, part of Iran's grain imports from Russia (trade_full/nonreport, ~USD 1bn/yr) is a third copy of the same value; not quantified, keep as a caveat or use in Iran's high case only. (6) Venezuela's repayments of Russian arms loans are debt service, not counted here; check that loans_value.json / russia_state_finance.json do not treat them as arms payments.
notes: The SIPRI Arms Transfers Database backend (atbackend.sipri.org) again reset connections; only the published fact sheets were used. Almost every new buyer value is an educated guess (D) built from contract news and SIPRI regional shares; individually they are small (all below EUR 0.4bn over 2022-2026), which is why they were left in ROW before. Rosoboronexport said Africa was >30% of its 2023 supplies. With Algeria and Egypt at EUR 0.93bn in russian_arms_exports.json and the African buyers assigned here at EUR 0.25bn, Africa is ~19% of the 2023 national total: either Algeria is too low (SIPRI warns it is) or more of the remaining ROW is African. The remaining 2023-2024 ROW is small (EUR 0.13 and 0.06bn), so a bigger Africa would have to come out of the named buyers. Sahel buyers (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger) and Libya pay MORE than expected, but their pivot to Russia follows coups and the French withdrawal, not the war in Ukraine; not_buyer_choice_share is reinterpreted for them (see note) and the builder may prefer to show them as labels only.
